name: Moldova
summary_text: Moldova is workable for trans visitors — the best-protected of the former-Soviet states outside the Baltics. Since 2022, anti-LGBT hate speech and hate crimes are criminal offences covering SOGI explicitly, the equality law was amended in 2023 to cover sexual orientation and gender identity, and Chisinau Pride marches through the city centre under police protection. Moldova is on the EU accession path, driving continued legal alignment. Counterweights: there is still no accessible legal gender recognition (a medicalised process exists on paper but Genderdoc-M reports it is not functional in practice), the Orthodox Church and major politicians (including Chisinau's mayor) regularly issue homophobic statements, and the breakaway Russian-controlled region of Transnistria has its own anti-LGBT "propaganda" law — travelers should treat Transnistria as a separate, much riskier jurisdiction.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Moldova: a trans woman was denied service at a bank due to document/appearance mismatch - the Equality Council confirmed discrimination; hate speech by politicians increased during election campaigns (Socialist Party newspaper: 'Ban on gay parades and LGBT propaganda in schools'); the location of GENDERDOC-M's Trans Camp was disclosed online, forcing relocation; hate crimes and domestic violence reported; civil society helped LGBT+ people fleeing Ukraine and Russia.

sources.title: Human rights in Moldova Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International Moldova report 2025: discrimination against LGBTI people remained commonplace; freedom of expression and assembly arbitrarily restricted; in Russian-occupied Transnistria new legislation prohibits 'promotion of non-traditional sexual relations'.

GENDERDOC-M report on the situation of LGBT+ rights in Moldova (2023): the Equality Council's 2022 study found extremely low acceptance - 79% of the population would not accept LGBT+ neighbours, 60% not as work colleagues; social distance score 5.7; marginalisation of LGBT+ people increased in 2022 amid pandemic, economic and security crises.

sources.title: Attitude revisit Moldova Pride 2024: a country slowly emerging from its past - Attitude
sources.claim_summary: Attitude (Feb 2026): revisits Moldova Pride 2024 - a country slowly emerging from its past to carve a new queer identity; participants of all ages and backgrounds join the festivities.

ECOM legislative analysis related to SOGI and HIV in Moldova (2024): identifies legal barriers affecting the quality of life of LGBT people and people living with HIV, based on a survey completed by local partners.

US State Department 2006 Human Rights Report for Moldova: documents police beatings, harsh prisons, societal violence and discrimination - baseline assessment including the situation of sexual minorities.

sources.title: Police in Moldova use tear gas on anti-LGBT protesters trying to disrupt Pride march | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (May 2018): police fired tear gas at anti-LGBT protesters to protect Moldova Pride in Chisinau; 20 embassies signed a statement of support for the march; President Dodon had publicly attacked the event the previous year.

sources.title: Moldova: Second largest city overturns local ban on 'gay propaganda' | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (March 2013): the Balti Court of Appeals struck down the city's 'homosexual propaganda' ban as unconstitutional and a human-rights violation, also criticising Balti's 'zone of enhanced support for the Orthodox Church' declaration - bans issued after church-led protests against the EU-backed anti-discrimination law.
